passage:
10:30 pm, Sunday. I finally did it: left the "Terrace Gang" chat. It had 300 messages a day, and my thesis chapter was suffering. But I did not want to slip out silently and have everyone wonder if I was upset.
So I wrote to Ojas, the admin, first: "Hey, I'm stepping back from the group till March to focus on my thesis. Nothing is wrong, I love you all. Ping me directly anytime." Then I left.
Ojas answered within a minute: "Understood! Good luck, we'll miss your memes ❤️" A few friends messaged me alone too. I feel light. And still wanted.
— Sarita

qa.q: What did Sarita write to Ojas before leaving the group?
qa.a: Sarita wrote that they were stepping back from the group till March to focus on their thesis, and that nothing was wrong.

qa.q: What was Sarita feeling about leaving the group at 10:30 pm?
qa.a: Sarita felt relieved and a little anxious about how it would look. Writing to Ojas first shows the wish not to hurt anyone.

qa.q: What did Sarita do that made leaving gentler than slipping out silently?
qa.a: Sarita wrote to the admin first, explaining the reason and saying nothing was wrong. Inviting friends to ping directly kept the friendships open.

qa.q: How might Ojas have felt to get the message before Sarita left?
qa.a: Ojas probably felt reassured and warm, since the reply came within a minute and mentioned missing Sarita's memes. Knowing it was not an insult made it easy to accept.

grounding: A person leaves a noisy group after telling the admin they are stepping back for focus, so it does not seem like an insult.

passage:
Group chat "Batch of 2019", Wednesday night
Jahnavi: Pradeep, you've been quiet, everything ok?
Pradeep: All fine 🙂 Just muting the group for a few weeks. Too many notifications while I prepare for my exam.
Jahnavi: Ah, got it. Leaving already?
Pradeep: Not leaving! Just muted. If something is urgent, tag me or call me.
Jahnavi: Perfect. Will tag you for the reunion plan 😄
Pradeep: Please do. I didn't want to just vanish and have you all wondering.
Jahnavi: Appreciated. Honestly, I thought you were upset with someone.
Pradeep: Not at all. Miss you all. Back in March, with snacks.
Jahnavi: Deal. Good luck with the exam!

qa.q: What reason did Pradeep give for muting the group?
qa.a: Pradeep said there were too many notifications while preparing for an exam.

qa.q: What was Jahnavi worried about when asking whether Pradeep was leaving?
qa.a: Jahnavi was worried that Pradeep might be upset or drifting away. The question "Leaving already?" shows the concern.

qa.q: What did Pradeep say that kept the friendship comfortable while muting?
qa.a: Pradeep said the group was only muted, not left, and asked to be tagged or called if something was urgent. The note "Back in March" kept the door open.

qa.q: How might Pradeep feel about the group while muting it?
qa.a: Still fond of everyone, since Pradeep says 'Miss you all', promises to be back in March with snacks and did not want to just vanish.

grounding: A person who wants out of a noisy group mutes it and tells the admin they are stepping back for focus, easing any hurt.

passage:
In their small town, the Ganesh festival committee's chat never slept. Pankaj had been added three years ago, and now it pinged at midnight with debates about pandal lights, forwards about sweets, and arguments over who had the drum schedule.
Pankaj was preparing for the state service exam. Every buzz broke his focus.
He knew what happened when Ramu left the group last year without a word: people said he'd become too big for the mohalla.
So he wrote to Sudha, the admin: "Sudha tai, I'm stepping back from the group till my exams in March. I'll still help on the festival day. Please call me if you need anything urgent."
Then he posted once in the group: "Taking a short break for exam prep. Missing you all already. Ganpati Bappa Morya!"
The replies came: folded hands, good luck wishes, one "Top karke aana!"
Pankaj muted the chat and opened his notebook.

qa.q: When are Pankaj's exams?
qa.a: His exams are in March.

qa.q: Why did Pankaj write to Sudha instead of just leaving?
qa.a: He was worried that leaving silently would look like an insult, as it had for Ramu, and he cared about staying on good terms.

qa.q: Which choice worked, and why?
qa.a: A private note to the admin plus one warm group message explained the break, so people wished him luck instead of feeling snubbed.

qa.q: How did the other committee members likely see his message?
qa.a: They felt warm and supportive rather than insulted, sending folded hands and good luck wishes.

grounding: A person steps back from a noisy group by telling the admin and posting a brief note, since silent leaving can seem an insult.

passage:
Thabo loved the Wednesday five-a-side games in Cape Town, but the team's chat was another thing. Two hundred messages a day about referees, old matches, memes, and who owed who a drink. He was starting a new job and his phone never stopped buzzing.
He thought about just leaving. But he remembered how, last year, the team had spent a whole evening guessing why Pieter had vanished from the group. Some said he was upset. Some said he'd found a better team.
So Thabo messaged Yosef, who ran the group: "Hey man, new job is eating my brain. I'm going to leave the chat for a bit so I can focus. Still coming Wednesdays. Can you text me if the time changes?"
Yosef replied: "Totally. Thanks for saying, bro. Most people just disappear."
The next Wednesday, Yosef shouted across the pitch, "Look who's still alive!" and passed him the ball.

qa.q: How many messages a day did the team chat have?
qa.a: The chat had two hundred messages a day.

qa.q: What was Thabo worried about if he left without a word?
qa.a: He was worried the team would feel insulted or confused and spend an evening guessing why he vanished, like they did with Pieter.

qa.q: What small step made Thabo's exit easy for everyone?
qa.a: Sending Yosef a short, friendly note that explained his focus and confirmed he'd still come on Wednesdays.

qa.q: How did Yosef feel about Thabo's message?
qa.a: Yosef felt appreciated and respected, saying thanks because most people just disappear.

grounding: A person who wants out of a noisy group tells the admin they are stepping back for focus, easing what could seem an insult.

passage:
The hospital's pharmacy staff had a social group called "Pharma Family", and it ran all day: birthday photos, lunch plans, a long thread about whose tiffin smelled best. Swati, who had just started night duty and was studying for her licensing exam, found it buzzing through her sleep.
At the staff canteen she stopped Trisha, who managed the group. "Trisha, can I tell you something before I do it? I'm going to leave Pharma Family for a while. Nothing wrong with anyone. I just need to sleep in the day and study."
Trisha laughed. "Thank God you told me. When Sudhir left last month, the whole group thought he was angry with us."
"That's why I'm telling you. And I'll post a short goodbye."
Her message went up that evening: "Stepping back for exams and nights. Please keep my birthday cake slice safe. 🙂"
Hearts and laughing replies followed.

qa.q: What was the social group called?
qa.a: The group was called "Pharma Family".

qa.q: Why did Swati want to tell Trisha first?
qa.a: Swati was worried that leaving silently would seem like anger, as it had when Sudhir left, and she cared about her colleagues' feelings.

qa.q: What could others learn from how Swati left?
qa.a: Tell the admin in person, give a simple reason like sleep and study, and post a short, light goodbye.

qa.q: How did Trisha feel when Swati explained?
qa.a: Trisha felt relieved and grateful, since Sudhir's silent exit had left the whole group thinking he was angry.

grounding: A person leaving a noisy group tells the admin and posts a brief note, since leaving silently can seem an insult in a close circle.

passage:
Hi Rekha,
Writing to you directly, since you set up our old building group and keep it going. I'm going to step back from it for the next few months. It's nothing anyone said. My CA final papers are in May, and right now I lose about an hour a day to the group, the birthday wishes, the cricket arguments, the forwarded jokes, and I can't stop checking.
I thought about just leaving quietly, but I know how that looks in a group like ours. Pinky aunty would decide I'm angry, and my mother would hear about it by evening 😅 So I'll mute it and post one line tonight saying I'm off to study and will be back after exams.
If anything important comes up, the water tank meeting or anyone's wedding, could you message me directly?
Thanks for understanding, and for always posting the sweets photos.
Sachin

qa.q: When are Sachin's CA final papers?
qa.a: They are in May.

qa.q: Why did Sachin decide against leaving the group quietly?
qa.a: Sachin was worried it would look like anger in such a close group, with Pinky aunty assuming a quarrel and word spreading by evening.

qa.q: What could Sachin's one-line post tonight say to keep things warm?
qa.a: Something like "Off to study, will miss the cricket fights, back after May!", so people know the quiet is temporary and not personal.

qa.q: How might Rekha feel reading this email?
qa.a: Rekha would likely feel respected and reassured, knowing the step back is about exams and not about anyone in the group.

grounding: Shows a person who wants out of a noisy group muting it and telling the admin about stepping back for focus, because leaving silently could look like an insult.
